items.title: Researchers observe orbital Nernst effect driven by heat
items.original_title: Heat drives electron orbital currents, revealing first experimental evidence of orbital Nernst effect
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Researchers have reported the first experimental evidence of a thermal transport phenomenon where a temperature gradient drives the transverse accumulation of electrons' orbital angular momentum, known as the orbital Nernst effect. By constructing a multilayer device using copper oxide, platinum, and a magnetic insulator, the team converted heat-generated orbital currents into measurable electrical signals. The experiments demonstrated that copper oxide exhibits a substantial orbital response that can be effectively translated and detected.
items.why: This demonstration provides insight into electronic band structures and establishes a potential pathway for utilizing waste heat in spintronic memory devices. The findings show that orbital transport could efficiently convert thermal energy into angular momentum.
technical_details: The researchers utilized a multilayer structure consisting of naturally oxidized copper film as the orbital source, platinum as a conversion layer, and yttrium iron garnet as the magnetic detector.
items.selection_reason: Reports the first experimental evidence of the orbital Nernst effect in Nature Communications, opening potential new directions in spintronics.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Researchers observe orbital Nernst effect driven by heat

items.title: High-frequency stimulated Brillouin scattering achieved in lithium niobate waveguides
items.original_title: High‐Frequency Stimulated Brillouin Scattering in Suspended Thin‐Film Lithium Niobate Waveguides
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Scientists have demonstrated stimulated Brillouin scattering in suspended thin-film lithium niobate waveguides, reaching high frequency shifts exceeding fifteen gigahertz. The platform exhibited large gain coefficients for these high frequency shifts when pumped at telecom wavelengths. This development helps address previous limitations in accessing high radio-frequency bands for integrated microwave photonics.
items.why: The suspended waveguide platform unlocks lithium niobate for scalable microwave photonics applications, including communications, sensing, and information processing. High gain coefficients and frequency shifts are key requirements for advancing integrated photonic filtering.
technical_details: The research utilized suspended Z-cut thin-film lithium niobate waveguides and applied spontaneous Brillouin microspectroscopy to confirm high-frequency acoustic modes.
items.selection_reason: Demonstrates high-frequency (>15 GHz) stimulated Brillouin scattering with high gain in suspended thin-film lithium niobate waveguides.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: High-frequency stimulated Brillouin scattering achieved in lithium niobate waveguides

items.title: US existing home sales fall to 16-year low
items.original_title: Home sales hit 16-year low in October amid soaring mortgage rates
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: US existing home sales dropped to 3.75 million units in October, marking a sixteen-year low. The decline was driven by high mortgage rates near a three-year high and rising inflation. Despite the drop in sales volume, the median existing-home sales price increased slightly to $416,700.
items.why: High borrowing costs continue to sideline prospective buyers and restrict housing market activity across multiple US regions.
items.selection_reason: Reports National Association of Realtors data showing US existing home sales dropped to a 16-year low in October due to high mortgage rates and inflation, representing a notable US economic development.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: US existing home sales fall to 16-year low

items.title: Nvidia Leadership Changes and Security Scrutiny
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Nvidia's security chief quietly departed in August, and CEO Jensen Huang stepped down amid scrutiny over his relationship with an executive at a firm linked to chip smuggling. The Singapore-based company Megaspeed stated that the executive, Alice Huang, left the firm in 2025 following investigations into chip smuggling to China. A former intelligence officer noted that corporate security teams are often poorly equipped to catch leaks involving everyday conversations.
items.why: The departure of key leadership and ongoing investigations highlight vulnerabilities in corporate oversight regarding export controls and high-tech supply chains.

items.title: Appeals Court Rules on New York Highway Funds
items.original_title: U.S. wrongly withheld New York highway funds over immigrant licenses, appeals court rules
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: A federal appeals court ruled that the U.S. Transportation Department wrongly withheld nearly $74 million in highway funds from New York state. The penalty was originally imposed after New York refused to revoke commercial driver's licenses for immigrants following an audit. The court concluded that penalizing the state was arbitrary and contrary to law because cancellation rules were not in place at the time.
items.why: This ruling clarifies federal authority and state obligations regarding commercial driver licensing regulations and infrastructure funding.
items.selection_reason: A federal appeals court ruled that the US Transportation Department unlawfully withheld $74 million in highway funds from New York over commercial driver's license policies.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Appeals Court Rules on New York Highway Funds

items.title: FAA Expands Artificial Intelligence Air Traffic Tool
items.original_title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration has expanded the deployment of an artificial intelligence tool designed to assist air traffic controllers. The system, called SMART, was initially used in airspace over Washington, DC, and is now being implemented across 22 centers nationwide. The agency reported that the initial rollout helped reroute flights, reduce fuel consumption, and save time.
items.why: Expanding automated traffic management systems aims to reduce national flight delays and improve fuel efficiency across commercial airspace.
technical_details: The system was deployed across all 22 centers following an initial rollout in the National Capital Region.
items.selection_reason: The FAA expands its $875 million SMART AI air traffic advisory tool across all 22 national air traffic centers following initial testing in Washington.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: FAA Expands Artificial Intelligence Air Traffic Tool

items.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for a drone attack targeting a U.S. military base in Bahrain. Bahrain's military stated that its air defense systems intercepted and destroyed the incoming drones before they achieved their objectives. The incident occurs amid an ongoing stand-off between the U.S. and Iran regarding control and shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

technical_details: The IRGC stated it targeted an air defense radar facility using six drones.

items.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare systems
items.original_title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare.
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Google Cloud has launched a new artificial intelligence platform designed to connect fragmented administrative and clinical medical systems. The software combines specialized data connectors to pull information from electronic health records, billing databases, and clinical guidelines. It aims to reduce paperwork and administrative burdens on healthcare staff by orchestrating multi-step workflows with human oversight.
items.why: The platform seeks to reclaim valuable staff time currently lost to administrative burdens and routine paperwork. It rolls out initially in preview alongside launch partners including major healthcare providers.
technical_details: The platform utilizes specialized skills and data connectors to integrate third-party systems.
It includes the Gemini Decisions API powered by the Gemini Decision model for calibrated multimodal decisions.
items.selection_reason: Google Cloud announces Gemini for healthcare, an AI platform designed to unify clinical systems and automate administrative tasks.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare systems

items.title: Trump's shifting Iran rhetoric leaves Middle East peace efforts in limbo
items.original_title: With shifting Iran rhetoric following U.S. elections, Trump leaves Middle East in limbo about path ahead
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Following midterm elections, President Donald Trump has issued contradictory statements regarding future U.S. military strikes and diplomatic talks with Iran. While suggesting the military conflict is effectively over and signaling a reduced need for a formal deal, he also maintained that the U.S. military remains ready to act. These mixed signals have complicated ongoing regional mediation efforts led by Qatar to restore secure shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
items.why: The president's ambiguous positioning creates uncertainty for international allies and regional diplomats attempting to negotiate an interim agreement for vital shipping lanes.
items.selection_reason: Reports shifting US foreign policy stances and diplomatic signaling regarding Iran following midterm elections.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Trump's shifting Iran rhetoric leaves Middle East peace efforts in limbo
